properties.name: Malaysia — palm oil and rubber gloves
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: Migrant workers on employer-tied permits with recruitment debt and retained passports. Several producers have been the subject of US withhold release orders, some later revoked after remediation — which makes this a useful case study in what remediation is actually required to look like.
properties.position: the place the anti-slavery map gives

properties.name: Top Glove — disposable gloves
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: WRO issued 15 July 2020 on gloves from Top Glove and TG Medical, escalated to a Finding, on indicators including recruitment-fee debt bondage among migrant workers. The company reimbursed recruitment fees and the order was modified. The clearest documented instance anywhere of an import ban putting money back into workers' hands — which is why it is on this map alongside the open cases.
properties.position: the place the anti-slavery map gives

properties.name: FGV Holdings — palm oil
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: WRO of 30 September 2020 covering palm oil and palm-oil products from FGV Holdings, its subsidiaries and joint ventures. CBP announced a modification on 15 January 2026. Palm oil passes through refiners and traders before it reaches a brand, so the trade-data lens is where this becomes actionable downstream.
properties.position: the place the anti-slavery map gives

properties.name: Sime Darby Plantation — palm oil
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: WRO of 30 December 2020, following a petition by Liberty Shared rather than a government investigation. CBP cited information indicating all eleven ILO forced-labour indicators. The route worth noting: an NGO petition, evidence on recruitment fees and document retention, then a ban.
properties.position: the place the anti-slavery map gives

properties.name: Taepyung Salt Farm — sea salt
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: WRO of 3 April 2025, following long-documented exploitation of workers with disabilities on South Korean salt farms. South Korea was one of four countries newly added to the 2024 US list of goods — a reminder that these determinations are not confined to low-income producing countries.
properties.position: the place the anti-slavery map gives

properties.name: Linglong International Europe — tyres
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: WRO of 18 December 2025. Notable because the workplace is inside Europe and the workers were Vietnamese nationals recruited for a manufacturing and construction site. The corridor pattern — recruited far away, indebted before arrival, isolated on site — does not stop at the EU border.
properties.position: the place the anti-slavery map gives

properties.name: Giant Manufacturing — bicycles
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: WRO of 24 September 2025 against one of the world's largest bicycle manufacturers, on indicators affecting migrant workers. Worth sitting with: a listed producer can be a well-known consumer brand rather than an anonymous subcontractor.
properties.position: the place the anti-slavery map gives

properties.name: Zhen Fa 7 — fishing vessel
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: WRO of 28 May 2025 on seafood from a single named vessel. At sea the unit of enforcement is the boat, not the company, which is why the flag and IMO registries matter as much as any corporate registry — and why AIS behaviour, months at sea without a port call, is what usually surfaces one of these. Placed at the flag state rather than at sea: a vessel can only be acted against through the registry it flies under and the port it enters, so that is the jurisdiction worth knowing.
properties.position: the middle of its country: CBP gives no place

properties.name: Da Wang — fishing vessel
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: WRO of 18 August 2020, later escalated to a Finding, which allows seizure rather than only detention. One of several Taiwan-affiliated vessels named from 2019, alongside Yu Long No. 2 (11 May 2020) and Lien Yi Hsing No. 12 (31 December 2020). Placed at the flag state rather than at sea: a vessel can only be acted against through the registry it flies under and the port it enters, so that is the jurisdiction worth knowing.

properties.name: Marange diamond fields
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: Rough diamonds from the Marange fields have been barred from US entry since the order of 30 September 2019, on evidence of forced labour in mining. A field-wide rather than company-wide order, which is the form these take where the production is not organised under oneoperator.

properties.name: Eastern DRC — artisanal gold
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: WRO of 30 September 2019 covering gold from artisanal small mines in eastern DRC. Issued the same day as orders on Marange diamonds, Malaysian rubber gloves from WRP Asia Pacific, and bone char from Brazil — five orders in one day, which remains the largest single action of its kind.

properties.name: Turkmenistan — cotton, country-wide order
properties.source: US CBP, as kept by the anti-slavery map (projects.json); CBP's own page refused this build
properties.desc: One of the few orders covering an entire country's output of a commodity: cotton produced anywhere in Turkmenistan has been barred from US entry since 18 May 2018, following a petition filed by the International Labor Rights Forum in April 2016. The harvest is state-mobilised, which is what makes a country-wide order the only coherent form.
